text: Some researchers have speculated that very frequent training sessions comprised of low per-session volumes may help to maximize the hypertrophic response. This hypothesis is based on the premise that the muscle protein synthetic response to a training bout is truncated as an individual gains training experience (55). Indeed, while muscle protein synthesis in untrained individuals remains elevated for ≥48 hours (177), trained lifters experience a higher initial peak response that returns to baseline after <28 hours (243). Based on these data, more repetitive stimulation of the muscle with higher weekly training frequencies would seem to allow for greater time spent in a net-positive protein balance, conceivably promoting a greater accretion of muscle proteins over time.
book: Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy
chapter: Chapter 4: Role of Resistance Training Variables in Hypertrophy
